title: The Last Recipe
premise: Rafael Zhou, twenty and eldest of four, has spent her life being careful: careful with money, with her siblings, with the family restaurant's fading legacy. When she finds her grandmother's recipe box hiding instructions that aren't recipes — steps that literally cook memory into food — she discovers the town of Marrow Bend was built on a tradition that trades memories for survival. The tradition is failing; the town is forgetting itself, and Rafael's own mother has already lost years to it. To save what remains, Rafael must decide how much of herself to feed the fire, ending with her choosing to preserve not the whole past but only what can be honestly carried forward — and rebuilding the recipe box from scratch.
about_author: Cyrus Hartwell grew up above his family's noodle shop in a coastal mill town, where he learned early that kitchens hold more than food. He writes stories about siblings, inheritance, and the quiet cost of holding a family together.

chapters.title: The Weight of Being First
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A chaotic morning: school forms, little brother Milo's asthma, mom's night-shift exhaustion. Rafael runs the household like a drill sergeant and resents no one out loud. Emotional beat: love expressed entirely through logistics, and the loneliness inside it.

chapters.title: What Grandma Left in the Tin
chapters.summary: Cleaning the shuttered restaurant, Rafael finds grandma Mei's recipe box. The last card isn't a dish — it reads like an instruction manual, addressed 'to whoever remembers.' POV Rafael. Beat: curiosity cracking open grief.

chapters.title: A Taste of Yesterday
chapters.summary: Following the card half-jokingly, Rafael cooks a soup and suddenly tastes a memory that isn't hers — grandma's, vivid and complete. Her sister Juno witnesses it. POV Rafael. Beat: wonder shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Rafael notices Marrow Bend's odd gaps: streets with no names, neighbors who can't recall their own weddings. Librarian Odette Voss confirms the pattern. POV Rafael. Beat: dread replacing wonder.

chapters.title: Mom's Missing Years
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts her mother, who admits trading memories to the tradition during hard winters — including chunks of Rafael's childhood. POV Rafael. Beat: betrayal and terrible understanding entwined.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the library basement, Odette shows Rafael the ledger: every founding family fed the fire, generation after generation. The Zhou name is on the first page. POV Rafael. Beat: inheritance revealed as debt.

chapters.title: Juno Wants In
chapters.summary: Juno, sixteen and furious at being protected, demands to learn the recipes. Their fight wakes the younger kids. POV Juno. Beat: sibling fracture — protection experienced as exclusion.

chapters.title: First Payment
chapters.summary: To stop a neighbor's total unraveling, Rafael cooks a payment dish and surrenders a memory of her father. It works — and she feels the hole where it was. POV Rafael. Beat: the price made personal.

chapters.title: Milo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Eight-year-old Milo reveals he's been dreaming the fire's location: under the old cannery, a hearth that predates the town. POV Milo. Beat: innocence carrying dangerous knowledge.

chapters.title: Down to the Hearth
chapters.summary: Rafael and Juno descend into the cannery and find the hearth — alive, hungry, shaped like a kitchen that shouldn't exist. POV Rafael. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: The hearth speaks through cooked dishes, offering a deal: one keeper per generation feeds it willingly, or it takes indiscriminately. Mom was this generation's keeper. POV Rafael. Beat: the trap of duty made explicit.

chapters.title: Odette's Confession
chapters.summary: Odette admits she was meant to be keeper before Mei took her place — and that Mei's death wasn't accident but exhaustion. POV Odette. Beat: guilt passed down like a recipe.

chapters.title: Running Out of Flavor
chapters.summary: The town's forgetting accelerates; a classmate vanishes from everyone's memory but Rafael's. Time pressure crystallizes. POV Rafael. Beat: urgency, isolation.

chapters.title: The Recipe That Wasn't Written
chapters.summary: Rafael realizes Mei left no successor card because she intended to break the cycle — the blank card is a message, not an omission. POV Rafael. Beat: grief reframed as permission.

chapters.title: Juno's Gamble
chapters.summary: Juno secretly cooks a payment to prove she can bear the burden, losing her memory of their father instead. Rafael finds out. POV Juno. Beat: sacrifice as rivalry, love as competition.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Wrong
chapters.summary: Desperate, Rafael attempts to cook a memory back into existence — restoring mom's missing years. The hearth accepts the dish but demands a life's worth in return. POV Rafael. Beat: hope weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Rafael prepares to give herself to the hearth, writing goodbye letters and teaching Juno the household routines. POV Rafael. Beat: calm resignation that reads as devastating.

chapters.title: The Siblings' Counter-Recipe
chapters.summary: Juno, Milo, and little Ada refuse the plan: they cook together, each contributing small memories voluntarily — shared, not surrendered. The hearth falters, unused to receiving freely. POV Juno. Beat: solidarity breaking the logic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Feeding the Fire Differently
chapters.summary: Climax. At the cannery, the Zhus offer the hearth a new covenant: celebrations instead of losses, feasts given in gratitude rather than extracted in fear. The hearth tests them brutally before accepting. POV Rafael. Beat: courage as collective act.

chapters.title: What Remains of Me
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Rafael takes inventory of what she lost and what she kept. Some holes stay empty; she learns to live beside them. Mom begins remembering in fragments. POV Rafael. Beat: mourning without despair.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: The family reopens the restaurant with a menu built from honest recipes — no magic, just food that holds people together. The town starts naming its streets again. POV Rafael. Beat: cautious joy.

chapters.title: The New First Card
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Rafael writes the recipe box's new first card: instructions for passing down without consuming. She hands the box to Juno — not as a burden, but as a choice. POV Rafael. Beat: identity reclaimed; the tradition survives by becoming kind.
